title: Friends, I'm officially calling it: algorithmic trading is entering a new era.
author: EAForexLab
selftext:
Today, an AI agent independently optimized a trading EA in MT5, analyzed the results, and performed cross-validation.

All on its own, without any involvement from me. While I was at the gym.

Were there some issues with the results? Absolutely. But here's the exciting part: many of them can be addressed by refining the prompts and improving the agent's workflow.

Not long ago, this kind of research would have taken hours of hands-on work. Now, a significant part of it can be delegated to AI.

Of course, none of this guarantees a profitable trading strategy. But the way we research, test, and optimize trading systems is changing right before our eyes.

Absolutely mind-blowing. And I think we're only getting started.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Cool that the agent ran the whole loop without you, that's a real time saver. The thing I'd check is how many settings it tried, since the screenshot shows a lot of passes and the top ones are often just the luckiest. Make sure the cross-validation used data the optimizer never saw, and see if the best settings still hold up when you nudge them a bit. Cymetica's Backtest Labs can keep the last 30% of history aside as out-of-sample, which is a simple way to do that check.

comments.author: fizzl13
comments.body: Cool workflow, and the hard part is exactly what you said: "problems with the results". A few thousand passes with profit factors in the teens on \~90 trades is what overfitting looks like, and an agent checking its own cross-validation won't catch that. What helped us: keep the last stretch of data out of the optimisation completely, let the agent pick one setting, then run it on paper live for a few months before real money. Also log every pass it threw away, not just the winner, so you can see how lucky the winner had to be.
